examples.trans: You gave me that advice yourself!

examples.text: До свидания, всего вам самого доброго.
examples.trans: Goodbye, all the very best to you.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Желаю всем приятного аппетита.
examples.trans: I wish everyone bon appetit.

examples.text: Можно всем, кроме нашего Вити.
examples.trans: Everyone is allowed, except our Vitya.

examples.text: Сижу спиной ко всем участникам.
examples.trans: I sit with my back to all the contestants.

справиться.gloss: to manage, to cope, to handle

meanings.en: to manage, to cope, to handle
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'правиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to manage', forming an aspectual pair with 'справляться'.

examples.text: Ладно, я сама со всем справлюсь.
examples.trans: All right, I will handle everything myself.

examples.text: Мы за два года тут не справимся.
examples.trans: We won't manage here in two years.

examples.text: Конечно, не справитесь. Вы же не я.
examples.trans: Of course you won't manage. You're not me, after all.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Он будет делать наше новое шоу.
examples.trans: He will produce our new show.

examples.text: Будем трудиться на общее благо.
examples.trans: We will work for the common good.

examples.text: А вы, шеф, будете там участвовать?
examples.trans: And will you participate out there, Chef?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.

examples.text: Класс, это вообще очень оригинально!
examples.trans: Awesome, that is really original!

examples.text: Нам очень приятно с вами познакомиться.
examples.trans: We are very pleased to meet you.

examples.text: Ничего очень страшного в этом нет.
examples.trans: There is nothing terribly bad in that.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'glad', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Я рада, что помогла тебе.
examples.trans: I am glad that I helped you.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, Елена Павловна, рад вас видеть.
examples.trans: Hello, Elena Pavlovna, glad to see you.

examples.text: Я была очень рада тебя увидеть.
examples.trans: I was very glad to see you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (root 'видеть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to see', forming an aspectual pair with 'видеть'.

examples.text: Я была очень рада тебя увидеть.
examples.trans: I was very glad to see you.

examples.text: Вот увидишь!
examples.trans: You'll see!

examples.text: Я увидел папу.
examples.trans: I saw Dad.
